title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
tagline: Two names the source never spells
summary: The freshness check added in 1.42.96 asks for the symbol's name on its line. A companion object is recorded under Companion and an object expression under a made up name, so both were declared out of date where they actually sit.

highlights.title: A companion keeps its documentation
highlights.description: The line reads companion object, with no capital C anywhere, so asking for the recorded name always failed.

sections.heading: Fixes
bullets: The freshness check knows the two names the parser invents and looks for the keyword instead. On a real Android project, asking every one of 47982 symbols for its documentation against an unchanged file now reports none as out of date, and shifting every file by one line still catches 96 percent of them.
